role: wave 3, domain 1 (collision with other replicators, MOVSW trails vs our MOVSB anchors), R2-measure, defense

method.static: agent2/night/scratch/B061/scan.mjs (call-far encodings, FF 1F immediates, A0-A7 IP-low immediates) plus a byte search for the A3-anchor patterns (al=A3 / ax=xxA3 / al=A1 followed by add word [bx],2).
method.dynamic: agent2/night/scratch/B061/fam.mjs reads warEnd.a45 in the two existing base traces (A4/A5 bytes each team wrote, by address mod 4). agent2/night/scratch/B061/cost.mjs counts FF A5 anchor deaths per cohort and gives an upper bound: score if the killed member had lived to the end with nothing else changed. The scoring formula matches scores.csv exactly.
method.probe: Paired probe: the MOVSW twin of rev0 (B051 cMovsw53: mov al,0A2h -> 0A3h in A, and in both places in B). Twin minus base for an opponent = net value of being in that opponent's family. This is two-way: their A5 kills our anchor, and our A4 trail kills their xxA3 anchor.
method.baseFixed: Opponent-side counterfactual: IND_cgx123123 converted to the MOVSB family (anchor xxA2; template prefixed with movsw; warrior 1 copies 9 words) against the unchanged base. The control re-assembly of cgx warrior 1 is byte-identical to the original.

prevalence.pool2025: 75 teams. Confirmed MOVSW 2-byte-call replicators (A5 written at residue 3 thousands of times per war; they wrote the A5 in all 80 first-push FF A5 anchor deaths in trace pkj3o): Y_TOM_Code_Killer (31 kills), A_IND_cgx123123 (22), A_WAN_Baltika9 (13), A_OHS_TrojanByte (10), A_WHS_K0F1M_AL_T1L1M (5). These are exactly the static A3-anchor hits (al=A3 / ax=xxA3; K0F1M uses al=A1 then add word [bx],2). Not MOVSW (a45): GGN_OpcodeHunter (A4 at residue 2, our family), OST_Gamma (A4 at residue 0), GhostBytes, TitanicSwimTeam. LowKey and BinaryBandits have no A3 anchor; probe effect -0.075 / -0.013, no sign of a net cost. The al=A1 lineage (HDS_YOY, OHS_TOMEX, GSA_B33, HRZ_Thingies, OHS_BatteringRAM, AML_ByteReapers, GSA_3Plate_Benchers, SZR_The_Chargers) is unclassified: these teams score <=0.10 vs base and the probe effect is inconsistent.
prevalence.pool2024final2: No static A3-anchor signature. In the probe, WHS_Lucas (+0.277, 4/0) and HRZ_SHRek (+0.138, 4/0) cost base more than they cost the MOVSW twin. GSA_OtoGlida (-0.417) and HRZ_Code_Killers (-0.438) crush the MOVSW family. Lucas is not a classic residue-3 trail: it pushes every 27h bytes, so its A4 cycles through all residues. The mechanism is unknown.
prevalence.chanceInRandom2025Cohort: P(a 3-opponent 2025 cohort contains >=1 of the 5 confirmed MOVSW teams) = 0.19; contains cgx123123 = 0.04

impact.traceUpperBound: Existing base traces: 82 of 161 base deaths are MOVSW anchor kills (pkj3o; 77 in 4sf0x). The upper bound in cohorts with a MOVSW killer is 0.10-0.29 points/battle (s2025-2 Code_Killer 0.258, s2025-3 cgx+Trojan 0.178, Baltika9+K0F1M 0.250, CodeKiller 0.117, TrojanByte 0.100, cgx 0.192). Cohorts without one: 0.
impact.cgxAsFiller: Every probe cohort that contains cgx123123, including 3 where it was only a filler (YOY#0 +0.175, B33#0 +0.40, IND_BRA#2 +0.25), favours the twin: 7/7.
impact.baseFixed_cgx: vyob8: base 0.558 (SE 0.037, 12 cohorts) vs original cgx; 0.708 (SE 0.037) vs MOVSB cgx. Difference +0.151, about 2.9 SE, unpaired cohorts with different fillers. The cgx team's own score barely moves (0.282 -> 0.238).
impact.fieldAverage: Net cost about 0.15-0.16/battle when cgx is present x 0.04 presence, plus at most about +0.003 from Baltika9 => about 0.006-0.01 points/battle on random 2025 cohorts (hypothesis, computed). Vs TrojanByte, base gains from the cross-family exchange.

threatFindings.threat: Exactly 5 of 75 2025 teams are MOVSW 2-byte-call replicators that kill our FF 1F anchor (Code_Killer, cgx123123, Baltika9, TrojanByte, K0F1M)
threatFindings.evidence: a45 residue-3 A5 counts and FF A5 kill writers in traces pkj3o / 4sf0x (fam.mjs, cost.mjs); static A3-anchor search finds the same 5 and no others

threatFindings.threat: cgx123123's cross-family collision costs base about 0.15-0.16 points/battle in cohorts that contain it
threatFindings.evidence: paired probe 1u12p +0.163 [0.079,0.246] 4/0, 7/7 cohorts with cgx favour the twin; base-fixed vyob8 +0.151 (~2.9 SE, unpaired)

threatFindings.threat: Code_Killer and Baltika9 cost base net points through the MOVSW anchor kill
threatFindings.evidence: 1u12p +0.025 [-0.060,0.110] and +0.075 [-0.089,0.239]. The kills are frequent (trace) but base wins the reverse collision often enough.

threatFindings.threat: TrojanByte / K0F1M exploit the MOVSB anchor net of the reverse collision
threatFindings.evidence: 1u12p TrojanByte -0.190 [-0.212,-0.167] 0/4 (base is better off in its own family); ar196 K0F1M -0.081 n.s.

threatFindings.threat: The field-average net cost of MOVSW collisions on the 2025 field is large
threatFindings.evidence: computed from the above: about 0.006-0.01/battle (upper bound before netting 0.10-0.29 in killer cohorts)

threatFindings.threat: 2024 finalists WHS_Lucas and HRZ_SHRek take extra points from base because of our MOVSB anchor residue
threatFindings.evidence: ucv7k: twin +0.277 [0.163,0.391] 4/0 vs Lucas, +0.138 [0.113,0.162] 4/0 vs SHRek. Lucas is not a residue-3 trail (27h push step); the mechanism is untraced.

threatFindings.threat: A byte-level anchor fix for FF A5 exists
threatFindings.evidence: analysis: jmp [di+d16] with d16 = attacker IPhi/CSlo and DI = anchor+1. DS must stay private for the template copy, and private segments lie above the arena, so the read faults about 97% of the time. Same conclusion as B051.

recommendation: Nothing to promote; no fix candidate. The MOVSW anchor kill is real and frequent (about half of traced deaths) but its NET cost on the 2025 field is small (about 0.006-0.01/battle) because base wins the reverse collision against most MOVSW teams. Only cgx123123 is a clear net loss (about 0.15/battle when present). Switching family is wrong: it loses about 0.42-0.44 vs 2024 finalists GSA_OtoGlida / HRZ_Code_Killers and 0.19 vs TrojanByte. Spend no more jobs on MOVSW anchor fixes. Suggested library additions: a 'movsw_cgx' focus for regression tests, and the 2024 finalists WHS_Lucas and HRZ_SHRek, which cost base 0.28 / 0.14 more than a MOVSW twin (mechanism untraced; a trace on a Lucas cohort is the next step).
